name: spinner
title: Spinner - FOC BLDC motor controller, STM32G431 + 3 x IR2104 / 60 V MOSFETs, MT6701, CAN FD
brief: Field-oriented-control BLDC motor controller for a 12-24 V bus: STM32G431KBT6 (LQFP-32) with an 8 MHz crystal and SWD on a 1.27 mm 2x5 Cortex header; a three-phase inverter of three IR2104 half-bridge drivers and six BSC028N06LS3 60 V MOSFETs, with a 10 mOhm low-side shunt per phase read by the MCU's internal PGAs; an on-board MT6701 magnetic encoder over SSI; CAN FD through a TCAN332G with two JST-GH ports and a switchable 120 R terminator; SMAJ24A TVS and 2 x 220 uF bulk on the input; AP63203 buck to 3.3 V and a 78L12 gate-drive rail; bus-voltage and NTC sensing; power, status and CAN LEDs; screw terminals for power and the motor; four M3 mounting points.

netClasses.name: VMBUS
netClasses.why: the motor supply. Its own class only for the via: a layer change in VM carries the whole bridge current, and a 0.7 mm drill (25 um plating) carries about 3.4 A at a 10 C rise by IPC-2221, where MOTOR's 0.5 mm carries about 2.7 A. A 1.4/0.8 mm via (3.7 A) left GND and U4_VB open at U4 in 4 of 4 routes (2026-10-01). VM is poured on In2 after routing (board.pours), so any stretch the router lays on In2 sits inside a plane, not a 1.5 mm inner track

netClasses.name: MOTOR
netClasses.why: phase and low-side-source copper. 1.5 mm is the widest track that still enters the IR2104's SOIC-8 VS pin and the MOSFETs' source pins next to their gates at 0.2 mm clearance (Freerouting runs without neck-down). IPC-2221 gives about 3.2 A for 1.5 mm of 1 oz outer copper at a 10 C rise, so the class is rated 3 A and is never narrowed

netClasses.name: PWR
netClasses.why: logic and gate-drive supplies: a few hundred mA at most; 0.4 mm enters the LQFP-32's 0.8 mm-pitch supply pins

rules.why_min_track: every class is 0.2 mm or wider; 0.15 leaves room for Freerouting's rounding

board.notes: 4 layers: F.Cu / In1 GND plane / In2 routing, then a VM pour / B.Cu. In1 is a Specctra power layer during routing; In2 stays a routing layer and gets its VM pour only after a measured 0 open. 3V3 is a few hundred mA and stays on its 0.4 mm tracks.

holes:H1?.why: M3 hole, top-left corner; locked first so nothing takes a corner

swd:J?.why: SWD header on the top edge above the MCU's SWD pins

mcu:U?.why: MCU in the logic corner; its right side (PWM, CAN) faces the power stage

vin:C1?.why: bulk capacitor on the bus column, by phases U and V

vin:C2?.why: bulk capacitor on the bus column, by phases V and W

motor:J?.why: motor leads leave the right edge, level with the middle phase

vin:J?.why: supply leads leave the bottom edge under the bus column

can:J1?.why: CAN in: GH mouth (the footprint's +y side) turned to face the left edge; the edge rung reads this part's mouth as +x

can:J2?.why: CAN out (daisy chain), below CAN in, mouth to the left edge. 0.5 mm lower than first placed, so its CAN word fits between the two ports (measured 2026-10-01: at y 37 the gap to J4's courtyard was 0.03 mm short, and the transceiver and the switch blocked the other spots)

can:SW?.why: terminator switch, lever (+y at rot 0) 0.85 mm proud of the left edge

buck:FB?.why: ferrite at the input terminal's VM pad, so the 1.5 mm bus copper ends there and only VM_F runs to the regulators

can:U?.why: transceiver between the MCU's FDCAN pins and the CAN ports

enc:U?.why: encoder in the low-profile lower-left area; the motor's magnet goes over it

ldo:U?.why: gate-drive regulator left of the bus corridor

buck:U?.why: buck beside the bus input, away from the encoder

vin:D?.why: TVS beside the input terminal's bus pad

sense:R1?.why: bus divider on the filtered bus, kept out of the bus corridor between the terminal and C2

sense:TH?.why: NTC at the W low side, clear of the phase corridors to the terminal

led_pwr:R?.why: LEDs along the top edge between the SWD header and the phase U driver

hb_u:U?.why: phase U driver above its MOSFETs

hb_u:Q1?.why: U high side: drain pad toward the bus column, source pins toward the low side

hb_u:Q2?.why: U low side: drain pad against the high side's source pins

hb_u:R1?.why: U shunt at the low side's source pins

hb_v:U?.why: phase V driver above its MOSFETs

hb_v:Q1?.why: V high side: drain pad toward the bus column, source pins toward the low side

hb_v:Q2?.why: V low side: drain pad against the high side's source pins

hb_v:R1?.why: V shunt at the low side's source pins

hb_w:U?.why: phase W driver above its MOSFETs

hb_w:Q1?.why: W high side: drain pad toward the bus column, source pins toward the low side

hb_w:Q2?.why: W low side: drain pad against the high side's source pins

hb_w:R1?.why: W shunt at the low side's source pins

route.why: the ladder is computed from each rung's opens; MOTOR carries a current budget so it is never narrowed; the outline is stated, so it is never grown

switches.why: 120R beside the throw that joins the terminator to CANL, OFF beside the open throw

polarity.why: J1 pin 1 is the bus (+). Measured 2026-10-01: no mark lands, because every spot the silk stage tries (1.9-2.3 mm from the pad centre) overlaps J1's own 2.8 mm pad. The vin block's silk list labels the pads +12-24V and - on the back instead; on the front J1's own footprint silk blocks those labels
